title: Online Level-wise Hierarchical Clustering

problem.claim: Hierarchical clustering must support incrementally arriving data in applications such as entity resolution and concept discovery.

gap.claim: Existing online hierarchical clustering algorithms generally have more limited accuracy and efficiency than scalable batch-setting counterparts, while batch algorithms do not apply directly to incrementally arriving data.

contributions.claim: A family of online hierarchical clustering algorithms combines high-quality trees with fast per-point insertion through a limited number of parallel non-greedy tree rearrangements.
The methods are analyzed under assumptions about the data and cluster separability.
The algorithms are used to build compressed prototypes for a k-nearest representative classifier.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The proposed algorithms reportedly achieve state-of-the-art results in hierarchical clustering dendrogram purity.
The proposed algorithms reportedly achieve state-of-the-art results in building compressed prototypes for a k-nearest representative classifier.

narrative_sequence.summary: Online hierarchical clustering typically trails scalable batch counterparts in accuracy and efficiency.
Incrementally arriving data is important in several clustering applications, but batch algorithms do not apply in that setting.
The paper introduces online algorithms using parallel non-greedy tree rearrangements to support high-quality trees and fast insertion.
The methods are analyzed under data and cluster-separability assumptions.
The authors report state-of-the-art results for dendrogram purity and compressed prototypes for a k-nearest representative classifier.

source_observation.claim: A limited number of parallel non-greedy tree rearrangements supports fast per-point insertion while maintaining high-quality trees.

interpretation.claim: Restricting structural updates while allowing parallel non-greedy adjustments may balance online efficiency and clustering quality.

application.claim: For streaming hierarchical clustering, consider bounded parallel structural repairs rather than fully greedy updates.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when the rearrangement strategy fails or how its assumptions limit applicability.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative accuracy, efficiency, or runtime results.
The abstract does not specify the data, cluster-separability assumptions, datasets, baselines, or experimental protocol.
